findings.description: [AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] The CORS policy that decides every outcome this test probes is statically verifiable and correct. CORSMiddleware is configured with allow_origins=settings.ALLOWED_ORIGINS - an explicit comma-separated allow-list from which config.py strips any '*' entry - so the wildcard-with-credentials combination the test targets cannot be produced even by operator error, despite allow_credentials=True. Starlette matches those origins by exact string, not regex or prefix, so the www-example.com / notexample.com / example.com.evil.com bypass classes do not apply. Methods and headers are enumerated rather than wildcarded. Anti-CSRF coverage for cross-origin requests is provided by CsrfMiddleware, which fails closed with a constant-time double-submit check on any unsafe method carrying an auth cookie. Authentication is enforced independently of Origin by the router-level dependencies in apis/router.py | verdict=pass confidence=high
